sections.title: Setting the speed of a story
sections.content: You know *cuando* and *mientras* from A2 Unit 13, *en cuanto* with the subjunctive from A2 Unit 27 and *a medida que* from B1 Unit 2. In a story, connectors also set the speed. *Apenas* and *en cuanto* make the second event follow the first at once. *Al cabo de* skips a stretch of time. *A medida que* and *conforme* show two things changing together, little by little. In a story about the past, all of them take the indicative.

sections.title: Fast, skipped and gradual
rows: Apenas: "as soon as", when a second clause follows. The second event comes at once. You know apenas "barely" from B2 Unit 1 (Apenas dormí, "I hardly slept"); before a clause with a second clause after it, it means "as soon as".
En cuanto llegó, llamó a su madre.
En cuanto: also "as soon as", with the preterite when both events are past.
Al cabo de dos horas, nos fuimos.
Al cabo de + a length of time: "after". The time in between is skipped.
A medida que subíamos, hacía más frío.
A medida que: "as", with the imperfecto. The cold grew while they climbed.
Conforme pasaban los días, se sentía mejor.
Conforme: "as", used like a medida que.

items.spanish: Apenas salí de casa, empezó a llover.
items.english: As soon as I left the house, it started to rain.

items.spanish: Al cabo de unos minutos, el niño dejó de llorar.
items.english: After a few minutes, the child stopped crying.

items.spanish: A medida que caía la noche, las calles se quedaban vacías.
items.english: As night fell, the streets emptied.

items.spanish: En cuanto llegamos al hotel, nos dormimos.
items.english: As soon as we got to the hotel, we fell asleep.

sections.content: Compare the future with the past. Looking ahead, *en cuanto* takes the subjunctive (A2 Unit 27): *en cuanto llegue* means "as soon as I arrive". In a story about the past it takes the indicative: *en cuanto llegué* means "as soon as I arrived".
